title: The RSI(2) dip buy on SPY won 3 of every 4 trades since 2000 and made a third of what holding did
author: person-person12
selftext:
RSI(2) is the dip buy that every swing trading channel gets to eventually, buy SPY when the 2 period RSI gets crushed and sell into the bounce. I ran it in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) on daily SPY candles from January 2000 to the end of March 2026 with a $10k start, with commission and slippage taken out of every trade.

**What it did:**

* 186 trades in 26 years, about 7 a year
* 75.8% winners
* profit factor 2.2
* $10k to about $21.4k, **+114% net**
* worst drawdown **14.9%**
* about $968 of the gross went to costs

Holding SPY over the same window took $10k to about $45.7k, **+357%**, with a **56.5% drawdown** on the way.

The win rate holds up and the curve is about as smooth as anything I've run on the index. It also made **roughly a third of what holding did**, and nearly all of that gap is time spent out of the market. It didnt take its first trade until May 2003 and it sat flat from December 2007 until the second half of 2009, which is where the small drawdown comes from and also where the missing return went, because it was still in cash for the first part of both recoveries.

The first ten trades were all held a week or less for a small gain each, so in a normal year the money spends most of its time sitting in cash while the index keeps compounding without it.
